strategy_game/docs/ISSUE_461_RESKIN_SPEC.md section 3.1: Transhumanity's Fate is a minimalist Fate Core conversion that 'avoided creating new concepts and wherever possible built off existing Fate Core concepts'

provenance.note: The schema and the mapping are this session's; the direction (a compact consolidated strategic list, mapped from the Fate-side skills) is issue #482's. Nothing here grants a bonus, sets a difficulty, or moves a quantity.

authoritative_vocabulary.note: Four of the proposed mission kinds below already exist in that vocabulary and keep their names. The four marked proposed are additions this roster needs in order to name a faction agent's covert, counter-intelligence and command missions at all; they are part of the same proposal and replace nothing.

strategic_skills.label: Statecraft
strategic_skills.definition: Moving people and institutions to the faction's position: negotiation, public argument, institutional access, the working relationship that makes either possible.
strategic_skills.overlaps: Overlaps command on a campaign run by leading from the front rather than by persuasion, and stewardship on gaining access through an organisation the faction already runs.
strategic_skills.terra_invicta_reference: The reference is persuasion: shaping the opinions of others. The scope here also carries the relationship and access side, which the reference treats through separate organisations.

strategic_skills.label: Fieldcraft
strategic_skills.definition: Acting unseen and uninvited: infiltration, surveillance, moving an asset, operating equipment where the faction is not supposed to be.
strategic_skills.overlaps: Overlaps security on counter-intelligence work, and inquiry when the point of the operation is to learn rather than to place something.
strategic_skills.terra_invicta_reference: The reference is espionage: moving in secret and conducting covert operations. This is the one skill whose whole scope has no counterpart in the six individual skills, which is why it needs a strategic layer at all.

strategic_skills.label: Inquiry
strategic_skills.definition: Finding out what someone would rather keep hidden, and reading what is already there: field investigation, records, forensics, the analysis of gathered material.
strategic_skills.overlaps: Overlaps science whenever the answer needs method rather than legwork, and fieldcraft when the evidence has to be taken rather than requested.
strategic_skills.terra_invicta_reference: The reference is investigation: discovering information someone would prefer to keep hidden.

strategic_skills.label: Stewardship
strategic_skills.definition: Running the faction as an organisation: members, money, offices, logistics, the standing relationships that let any of it happen.
strategic_skills.overlaps: Overlaps statecraft on access gained by argument rather than by administration, and command when the organised body is a security or field detail.
strategic_skills.terra_invicta_reference: The reference is administration: managing large organisations.

strategic_skills.label: Command
strategic_skills.definition: Leading the faction's people where it counts: directing a field operation, holding a contested position, taking part in violence when the faction has committed to it.
strategic_skills.overlaps: Overlaps security on operations whose purpose is protection rather than action, and statecraft on a campaign that is won by argument rather than by presence.
strategic_skills.terra_invicta_reference: The reference is command: organizing and leading combat operations. No numeric scale, odds or action economy is taken from it.

strategic_skills.label: Science
strategic_skills.definition: Research and analysis: adopting and adapting a technology, and deriving a new understanding of a phenomenon the faction only partly grasps.
strategic_skills.overlaps: Overlaps inquiry on the difference between a method and a case file, which is a design question rather than a settled boundary.
strategic_skills.terra_invicta_reference: The reference is science: investigating and analysing phenomena to derive new understanding.

strategic_skills.label: Security
strategic_skills.definition: Surviving and preventing harm to the faction's people and holdings: counter-intelligence, hardening an asset, holding under interrogation or attack.
strategic_skills.overlaps: Overlaps fieldcraft on the covert work done against the faction rather than for it, and command when protection turns into an operation.
strategic_skills.terra_invicta_reference: The reference is security: the ability to survive violence. The scope here adds counter-intelligence, because in this setting the faction's exposure is usually informational before it is physical.

proposed.covert_action: A mission that must not be attributable to the faction: infiltration, surveillance, placing or moving an asset.
proposed.counterintelligence: A mission that protects the faction's people or holdings from another faction's covert action, or recovers what was taken.
proposed.field_command: A mission that commits the faction's people to a contested place, with or without violence.

proposed_mission_kinds.note: No mission carries a difficulty, a cost, an odds, a duration or an effect here. Those are #323's and the author's.

mapping_caveats: The source column of `mapping` names Fate Core's skills. That table was prepared before Transhumanity's Fate's own list was verified; `transhumanitys_fate_mapping` now carries that list, recorded from secondary sources as names only.

Fate Core is CC BY 3.0 and its skill names are used here as design references only: the eighteen rows are a consolidation into seven NoöPunk skills, not a reproduction of Fate Core's skill descriptions.
The individual layer's crosswalk (the six skills, and where a Fate Core skill goes when the character acts alone) is documented in strategy_game/RULEBOOK.md section 4 rather than duplicated here.
not_imported_from_terra_invicta: The numeric attribute scale and any attribute value.
Mission success probabilities, weights or modifiers.

The action economy: TI's councilor count, its recruitment cost in influence, its XP award per mission and its turn cadence. Issue #482 states the crossover's own structure (one leader and four agents, at most one action per character per turn) and it is not TI's.
Councilor professions, traits, orgs, detection and intel mechanics.

TI's eighth attribute, loyalty, is not a skill here: it describes a character's relation to their faction, and this repository already models relations as edges (strategy_game/relationships.py). Turning it into a skill would make betrayal a check the character rolls rather than a thing that happens to the fiction.

terra_invicta_model.source: https://wiki.hoodedhorse.com/Terra_Invicta/Councilors and /Missions (read via the wiki's own raw and mirrored pages; direct access is Cloudflare-blocked)
verified: A councilor has eight attributes and there is no separate 'skill' tier: a contested mission compares an attack stat against a defence stat, both drawn from those same eight attributes.

The eight are persuasion, investigation, espionage, command, administration, science, security and loyalty, and each carries a family of missions -- the reference column terra_invicta_missions names them per proposed skill.
A councilor's usable mission set also comes from a profession and from equipped organisations, so 'which missions may this councilor attempt' is not a function of the attributes alone.
Missions are assigned in an assignment phase; some resolve automatically and the contested ones are rolled.

Loyalty is used as the defence stat of two missions and describes how likely a councilor is to defect to another faction -- which is why this proposal keeps it out of the roster (see not_imported_from_terra_invicta).
unverified: That a councilor attempts exactly one mission per assignment phase. The official wiki implies it through its intel wording but does not state it, and the statements found elsewhere were secondary sources. The crossover's one-action-per-character turn comes from #461/#482 and depends on none of this.
Detention, protection and campaign-calendar durations: these exist in the game's own data and are deliberately not reproduced.
The alien and Servants factions' roster rules -- their council size, and whether they recruit from the same candidate pool.
terra_invicta_model.not_reproduced: No attribute value, mission weight, probability, cost, duration or action-economy quantity is recorded here or anywhere in the crossover material, and no wiki text is quoted.

transhumanitys_fate_mapping.note: Movement, balance and defence at scene scale.
Contacts and services outside the faction: influence held as a relationship, which is exactly what a strategic negotiate or campaign turn spends.
Operating under a false identity is the covert mission, not a scene check.
Financial leverage is an organisational resource; at scene scale its use reads Savvy.
Scene-scale manipulation.
Influence inside one's own organisation, which is what a leadership mission draws on.
Melee and close combat.
Building, repairing and demolition are hands-on: scene scale. A construction programme is a stewardship mission instead.
Feeds both: the scene check is the movement, the mission is acting uninvited. Renamed from Stealth by TF; this edition folds the scene half into Reflexes.
Feeds both: intrusion and countermeasures at scene scale read Cognition; running a cyber mission needs the netrunner capability, which is a permission rather than a skill.
Feeds both, and the split is the issue's own example: finding something out in a scene is individual, mounting an investigation as an agent is strategic.
Reading people: TF's replacement for Empathy.
Care at scene scale; a public-health programme would read Science.
Awareness.
Vehicles and remote operation.
Writing and modifying code; the cyberattack capability gate is separate, and it is not a skill.
Coercion at scene scale; as an organisational lever it would read Statecraft, which is a design proposal.
Creating relationships and positive feeling.
Ranged combat.
TF's own strength-and-endurance skill. Kept as SOM; the Fate Core Physique beside it does not survive.
Endurance, orientation and movement through hostile environments.
Composure under pressure, including horror and psi. Kept as WIL; the Fate Core Will beside it does not survive.
Feeds both: knowing the species is individual; advising a contact policy is a scientific mission.
Feeds both: knowing the threat is individual; assessing it for the faction is a security mission.

transhumanitys_fate_mapping_finding: Almost the entire TF list is scene-shaped: it consolidates into the six individual skills. Only three TF skills are organisational by nature (Civ Rep, Eye Rep, Cred), and most of the rest can feed a mission as well as a scene. The seven proposed strategic skills therefore cannot be derived from TF's list - that layer is a design choice informed by Terra Invicta's shape, which is why D22 is a ruling and not a merge. This mapping answers the review the issue asks for; it approves nothing.
